source_evidence: If you invest in a variable annuity through a tax-advantaged retirement plan, such as an IRA or a 401(k) plan, you get no additional tax advantage from the variable annuity.
answer: A variable annuity held inside a tax-advantaged retirement account, such as an IRA or 401(k), does not provide an additional tax advantage from the annuity itself. The annuity still has its own investment options, insurance features, fees, and risks, so understand those terms separately from the retirement account’s tax treatment.
